name: Two-colourings of K11 with few edge-disjoint monochromatic triangles
description: construct() -> {'n': 11, 'colors': [...]}: colour 0 or 1 for each of the 55 pairs (i,j), i<j, in lexicographic order. The score is the maximum number of edge-disjoint monochromatic triangles, computed exactly per colour by branch and bound. Minimize; the known optimum is 6. Any colouring gives an upper bound on the minimum; the tabulated value for n = 11 is 6.

name: Large graphs with no regular induced subgraph on six vertices
description: construct() -> {'n': n, 'edges': [[u, v], ...]}: a simple graph on vertices 0..n-1 with 1 <= n <= 22. No set of 6 or more vertices may induce a regular subgraph (every vertex subset is checked). Maximize n. A valid graph on n vertices certifies G(6) > n. Graphs with 20 vertices are known; a 21-vertex graph would show G(6) >= 22.

sources.locator: Paul W. Dyson and Brendan D. McKay, Ramsey numbers for regular induced subgraphs (2026). arXiv record inspected; Erdős Problem #82 page inspected: G(5) = 17, G(6) >= 21 and G(7) >= 30 (Alexeev and McKay; Dyson and McKay), where G(k) is the least order forcing a regular induced subgraph on k vertices. OEIS A392636 inspected: graphs on 20 vertices without regular induced subgraphs of order 6 exist; whether any exist on 21 vertices is unknown. A valid graph on n vertices certifies G(6) > n. Graphs with 20 vertices are known; a 21-vertex graph would show G(6) >= 22.
Erdős Problem #82 (open); statement, history and current bounds reviewed 2026-09-24.

limitations: The five-vertex starter is trivial. Verification enumerates all vertex subsets, so n is capped at 22.

name: Edge-colourings of K16 in which every K4 sees five colours
description: construct() -> 120 integer colours in 0..119 for the pairs (i,j), 0<=i<j<16, in lexicographic order. Every set of four vertices must span edges of at least five distinct colours. Minimize the number of colours used. A valid colouring certifies f(16) <= colours used. The general bounds give 13 <= f(16) <= 15; no exact value for n = 16 is documented.

sources.locator: Paul Erdős and András Gyárfás, A variant of the classical Ramsey problem (1997). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #136 page inspected: Erdős and Gyárfás proved 5(n-1)/6 < f(n) < n and f(9) = 8; Bennett, Cushman, Dudek and Prałat proved f(n) ~ 5n/6. A valid colouring certifies f(16) <= colours used. The general bounds give 13 <= f(16) <= 15; no exact value for n = 16 is documented.
Erdős Problem #136 (solved (f(n) ~ 5n/6)); statement, history and current bounds reviewed 2026-09-24.
